## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call is supported over the runners-up. At 3 µM tubulin is lost (tub_mean z=-5.11, act_tub_ratio z=+8.52) with visual loss of filamentous microtubules (e6) and a monotonic tub_mean decline across 0.1-3 µM (rho=-1.0, e10) plus monotonic cell loss (e13); this argues against Actin disruptors, where actin itself is instead brighter/more textured (act_mean z=+6.38), and against Aurora inhibition, which would enlarge nuclei while nuc_area falls (z=-9.15, e14). The 3 µM atlas is dominated by Microtubule destabilizers (6/10, top similarity 0.913, e7); Epithelial neighbours are close in similarity but do not explain the filamentous-tubulin loss described in e6. The extreme nuclear/actin changes rest on a single high-dose well, but the key tubulin and cell-count trends are corroborated across four independently acquired dose wells, so a replicate is unlikely to overturn the call. Probability 0.80 is calibrated given the atlas ambiguity and the phenotype caveat about secondary microtubule loss.

## Unblinding

Compound: **colchicine** (PubChem CID [6167](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6167))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Tubulin inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Microtubule destabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule destabilizers**.

## Reflection

The call of Microtubule destabilizers was driven by convergence of the 3 uM well showing severe nuclear shape distortion with tubulin loss, visual loss of filamentous microtubules on describe_phenotype, and a 6/10 atlas match to Microtubule destabilizers, corroborated by monotonic tub_mean decline rho=-1.00 and monotonic cell loss rho=-1.00 across four doses with rising act_tub_ratio.

What misled was the second atlas at an intermediate dose mapping to DNA damage 6/10 and DNA replication 3/10, plus non-significant dose trends for nuc_solidity rho=-0.40 p=0.6 and act_std rho=+0.20 p=0.8, showing that nuclear size increase at 0.1-1 uM and mitotic-like features can mimic other classes before full depolymerization. The extreme phenotype rested on a single high-dose well with only 157 cells versus 424-545 cells at lower doses, making selection and cytotoxicity artifact a real risk.

Probability 0.80 was appropriately cautious given Epithelial and Actin neighbours in the first atlas and the single-well basis for nuclear collapse, but correctly weighted the tubulin-selective trend over actin and the fall in nuc_area at high dose against Aurora enlargement.

What was right:
- Acquiring the 3 uM maximal well first revealed extreme nuclear irregularity nuc_solidity z=-36.0 and nuc_area z=-9.2 that anchored dose comparison (e2)
- Microscopist visual of lower density with loss of filamentous microtubules suggested Microtubule destabilizers (e6)
- High-dose atlas 6/10 Microtubule destabilizers discriminated against Actin disruptors and Epithelial neighbours (e7)
- Monotonic tub_mean decline rho=-1.00 p=0 plus rising act_tub_ratio rho=+0.80 and monotonic cell loss rho=-1.00 argued selective microtubule loss (e10, e12, e13)
- Correctly rejected Aurora kinase inhibitors because nuc_area fell at high dose and dose trend was negative rho=-0.80 rather than enlarged (e2, e14)

What was wrong or missed:
- Underweighted the intermediate-dose atlas mapping to DNA damage 6/10 and DNA replication 3/10, which showed mitotic arrest features overlap other MoAs (e11)
- Over-interpreted nuclear shape collapse from dose_response of nuc_solidity rho=-0.40 p=0.6 and act_std rho=+0.20 p=0.8, both non-significant across only 4 wells (e8, e9)
- Acquisition plan used only 4 single-replicate wells at 0.1-3 uM with 157 cells at 3 uM versus >400 at lower doses, leaving the key tubulin-loss and extreme nuclear phenotype without a high-dose replicate and no lowest-dose baseline (e1, e2, e3, e4)
